learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge about the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Ability to work effectively in a team.
Ability for motivation for achievement and continuous improvement.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Will be able to solve a medium-difficulty automation problem using ladder diagram language (KOP).
Will be familiar with the most commonly used sensors and actuators at an industrial level.
Will master the terminology of the field of process control.
Will be able to solve problems related to the analysis, modeling, and control (PID strategy) of continuous, linear, and time-invariant systems.
At a basic level, have the ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to industrial automation and control systems
Programming programmable logic controllers in Ladder Diagram (KOP) language
Programming practicals in KOP language with Siemens S7-1200 PLCs
Time and frequency response of continuous systems
teaching_methods: Practical sessions in computer lab and/or laboratory

assessment_methods.method: Development test (Single Assessment: theoretical aspects of both blocks)
Practical test (Single Assessment: practical content of both blocks)

assessment_rules: For Continuous Assessment, the final grade (CF) is calculated as 0.35*PD1 + 0.35*PD2 + 0.15*PR1 + 0.15*PR2. To pass, a minimum of 3.5 points must be obtained in each of PD1, PD2, PR1, and PR2, along with a minimum global practical grade (PR=(PR1+PR2)/2) of 5 points and a minimum global theoretical grade (PD=(PD1+PD2)/2) of 5 points. If any minimum requirement is not met, the final grade will be 4.5. For Single Assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.70*PT + 0.30*PP, and both tests (PT and PP) must be taken. Practical activity grades from the previous year may be retained if minimum requirements (PR1 >= 3.5, PR2 >= 3.5, PR >= 5) are met.
